method.label: Add the times for equal distances

annotationRationale: The equal distances and distance-speed-time relationship produce a linear equation for the walking distance. Solving requires clearing numerical denominators, converting minutes to hours, and rounding the result.
sourceMethod: Follows the official MAA method of assigning distance d to each half of the trip and adding the two travel times. The equation is solved explicitly using a common denominator.

review.mathCheck: The equal half-distances give d/17+d/5=44/60. Hence 66d=187 and d=17/6 kilometers, which rounds to 2.8, choice C. Units and the requested walking distance are handled correctly.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Matches official solution 4 on attached page 2: define the common half-distance and add the two travel times. The wording is independently recast, with correct intermediate algebra added.
review.annotationCheck: p111 and 045 appropriately assess the rate relationship and equation model. The denominator, time-conversion and rounding nodes correctly describe supporting knowledge.
